rows.why: Item 11 asks how Monday is judged and in which time zone. The pick formats the instant as a weekday in the given zone. That makes 16:30Z, which is Monday 00:30 in Singapore, due, and 15:59:59Z, still Sunday there, not due.

The DST case is the same question: which local day it is in the given zone. Formatting the instant with the zone's rules handles the March 8 clock change. Monday 00:30 New York time counts as Monday and Sunday 23:59:59 does not.

This scenario covers several things (furthest gate, gate 0 with no submissions, merged tasks left out). The closest single item is how the furthest gate is computed. Taking the highest gate over all submissions gives 2 for submissions at gates 1 and 2. Items 7 (gate 0) and 1 (open only) also agree with their parts.
Item 6 asks how age is computed and rounded. Whole elapsed days rounded down give 9 for 9 days 23 hours and 10 for exactly 10 days.

The core rule is '14 days or more', which settles the boundary question in item 3. The >= comparison matches it. The scenario also settles item 4 (measure from posting when there are no submissions) and item 5 (measure from the latest submission), and both picks agree.
Item 9 asks about digest order. The pick puts stalled tasks first, then oldest postedAt, then id ascending, which is what the scenario expects.
Item 10 asks about the subject format and plurals. The scenario wants '1 open task' for a single task, but the pick always uses the plural.
Item 2 asks what buildDigest returns when nothing is open. Returning null means no digest at all rather than an empty one, which the scenario expects.

The scenario says an unknown zone fails, with no condition on whether tasks are open. That settles item 12's question: validate the zone in every case. The pick validates first and throws. The pick does not say whether the error names the zone.
